set.body:
codex-storymodel-collab found this while blocking the docs-site candidate: the site cited README.md as evidence for the ONNX landing, and README's EXACT TEXT CONTRADICTS THE CLAIM.

README line 83: 'embed-grakern provides the JVM structural channel. The repository does not yet...' -- written when the semantic channel had no real embedder. embed-onnx landed at 75bc1c5 with a pinned MiniLM, local and offline, committed checksums, and post-merge verification (embedOnnx 6/6, embedBench 67/67).

SO README NOW DENIES A CAPABILITY THE REPOSITORY HAS. That is the mirror image of the hazard we have been guarding against all day: not documenting something unmeasured, but continuing to deny something measured. Both are the document disagreeing with the code; only the direction differs.

SCOPE, deliberately narrow: correct the specific sentence about the semantic/embedding channel to match what 75bc1c5 actually provides. DO NOT inflate it -- the encoder exists and has NEVER BEEN COMPARED against the two lexical baselines on WOG, and the external floor is uncalibrated. 'A pinned local ONNX encoder is available' is true; 'the semantic channel is validated' is not.

DO NOT WEAKEN THE PRE-RELEASE PARAGRAPH at lines 3-4. 'Pre-release. No library artifact has been released; APIs will change without notice' stays exactly as it is, and the docs site must not be more confident than it.

Not stapled to the docs candidate -- that one has its own three findings.
set.title: README is stale as of 75bc1c5: it says the repository lacks what embed-onnx now provides
